# The Wire

Every message on the bus is a single contiguous buffer: a fixed 256-byte header followed by an opaque payload. NNG pub/sub prefix-matches on the topic field at the start of the header.

## Header

```c
typedef struct __attribute__((packed)) {
    char     topic[32];          // subscription prefix — at offset 0 for NNG prefix match
    uint8_t  id[16];             // uuidv7 binary — monotonic, time-ordered
    uint8_t  correlation_id[16]; // stable across entire causal chain
    uint8_t  causation_id[16];   // direct parent tuple id
    char     origin[32];         // actor id that emitted this tuple
    int64_t  emitted_at;         // unix nanoseconds
    int64_t  ttl;                // nanoseconds until expiry; 0 = no expiry
    int32_t  attempt;            // retry count; 0 = first delivery
    uint32_t payload_len;        // bytes following this header
    uint8_t  _reserved[120];     // pad to 256 bytes
} actor_header_t;
```

::: {.callout}
**Zero copy.** The runtime casts directly to `actor_header_t` from the NNG message body — no allocation, no parsing, no branching. `__attribute__((packed))` guarantees layout. Cast and read.
:::

## Payload

The bytes after the header are **opaque** up to 1 MB. The runtime never inspects them. Handlers negotiate their own encoding — MessagePack, Protobuf, raw text — without any runtime change.

## Causal chain

Three IDs travel with every tuple:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | Identity of this specific tuple. UUIDv7 — monotonic, time-ordered. |
| `correlation_id` | Stable across an entire request chain. All tuples belonging to one user request share the same value. |
| `causation_id` | The `id` of the direct parent tuple — one hop back in the chain. |

This is not a logging convention — it is a structural guarantee baked into the header. Every tuple the runtime emits carries the `correlation_id` and `causation_id` of the tuple that caused it. The chain is complete by construction.

A concrete ReAct turn produces this graph:

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
  participant C  as client
  participant AG as agent
  participant ST as worker

  C  ->> AG : id=A  corr=X  caus=—
  AG ->> ST : id=B  corr=X  caus=A
  ST ->> AG : id=C  corr=X  caus=B
  AG ->> C  : id=D  corr=X  caus=C
```

Every tuple shares `corr=X`. Each `causation_id` points one hop back. A subscriber on `*` that records every tuple can reconstruct the full execution graph of any request — across any number of actors, any number of hops — with no tracing infrastructure, no sidecar, no instrumentation. The bus is the trace.
